answers.answer: An HTTP cache stores response bodies and metadata (status and headers) for reuse. A browser private cache serves its user agent; a CDN provides shared edge caches near users. Origin is the server responsible for the resource. A hit finds and reuses a suitable stored response; a miss lacks a usable one. Empty: browser → CDN → origin; response origin → CDN → browser, stored only where policy permits. A browser hit answers locally without a network request. Another browser missing locally can get a CDN hit, avoiding origin. Caches store HTTP responses, not database records: origin may query a database, but hits need not reach either. CDN request hit ratio is hits/requests at that CDN: 800/1000 = 80%; the other 200 cause 200 origin requests under the stated assumptions. Browser hits never reached this denominator. Different response sizes mean this is not bytes saved; validation, background requests, extra layers and application/database work must be measured separately in real traffic. Repeated public assets can gain nearby delivery latency, lower origin requests and transfer. CDN requests/transfer can cost money; keys, invalidation and monitoring cost operational work. For low-traffic mostly private or rarely reused Notes responses, omit shared caching if measured reuse, latency and total-cost benefits do not justify costs; keep privacy policies intact. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: An HTTP cache stores response bodies and metadata, such as status and headers, for reuse.
A browser hit avoids the network request. After a browser miss, a CDN hit avoids origin.
The ratio is 800 / 1,000 = 80%.
For a low-traffic application serving mostly private or rarely reused responses, omit shared caching if measured benefits do not justify those costs.

answers.answer: Cache-Control carries response caching directives. public explicitly permits shared caching subject to other rules. max-age=60 gives a 60-second freshness lifetime; s-maxage=300 overrides that only for shared caches. Fresh means young enough for policy-authorized reuse without validation; stale means the freshness limit was reached, not that the body was deleted. Age estimates seconds since origin generation or successful validation, including time through caches. At Age 90 the browser is stale by 30 seconds (60−90 = −30, no fresh lifetime remaining); CDN remains fresh for 300−90 = 210 seconds. Delivery does not reset the clock, and freshness does not prove origin unchanged. A representation is the resource’s returned form. Revalidation checks whether a stored representation remains usable. ETag is an opaque representation validator preserved as given. If-None-Match sends that validator in a conditional GET to ask for a body only if the selected representation no longer matches. Stale CDN sends GET to origin with If-None-Match: "v1". If unchanged, origin returns 304 Not Modified with no replacement body; CDN updates applicable metadata including freshness and serves its retained v1 body to the ordinary browser GET. If changed, origin returns 200 with new body and ETag "v2"; CDN serves the new body and replaces its stored representation if permitted. ETags do not push updates to other caches. 304 saves body transfer on the validation hop but needs a network round trip to origin; origin may execute application logic and query its database. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: The CDN has 300 − 90 = 210 seconds of freshness left.
Freshness is permission to reuse, not proof that origin content is unchanged.
It sends a conditional GET to origin with If-None-Match: "v1", asking for the body only if the selected representation no longer matches.
The CDN updates applicable stored metadata, including freshness information, and uses its retained body to answer the browser's ordinary GET.
Origin was still contacted and may run application logic or query a database to decide whether the representation changed.

answers.answer: Cookies are browser-held state; Set-Cookie asks the browser to store it and Cookie sends it back. Authorization is the request header carrying credentials. Authentication establishes identity; authorization checks permission to access the resource. Choose unqualified Cache-Control: no-cache for the public page: storage allowed but successful validation required before every reuse. Choose Cache-Control: private for browser-allowed private notes: shared-cache storage prohibited, browser storage allowed subject to other directives, without inherently requiring validation each reuse. Choose Cache-Control: no-store for sensitive notes: HTTP caches instructed not to store. It cannot erase earlier delivered copies or replace permission checks. Cookie and Set-Cookie neither automatically partition per-user entries nor universally prevent caching. Authorization-bearing requests have special shared-cache restrictions, but response policies can permit reuse; authentication is not a universal bypass. A shared response reused for another user can expose private notes. Keep authorization at origin, explicitly apply private/no-store as appropriate, verify actual CDN rules prevent shared storage and reuse, and test different users. Do not make personalized responses public to improve hits. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: Cookies are browser-held state: Set-Cookie asks the browser to store it; Cookie sends it back.
no-cache means validate; no-store means do not store; private excludes shared caches.
Cookie and Set-Cookie do not automatically create per-user cache entries or universally prevent caching.
For private routes, verify that explicit private/no-store policies and actual CDN rules prevent shared storage and reuse.

answers.answer: A cache key identifies the stored response that can satisfy a request. A representation variant is a different returned form of the same resource. HTTP matching uses method and target URL plus selected request headers for variants. Keep format=pdf distinct from format=html and en distinct from fr. Vary specifies request headers whose values must match for reuse; Vary: Accept-Language separates language variants when supported and honored. If CDN ignores queries, verify actual matching configuration retains the meaningful format values and language distinctions; fix that or bypass caching until it does. Dropping format can return HTML to a PDF request; dropping language can return the wrong language. Keeping irrelevant tracking parameters multiplies entries and reduces hits; exclude only after confirming they do not affect the response. Vary does not alter the URL, grant access permission or override private/no-store; separating public variants never authorizes sharing private notes. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: A cache key identifies which stored response can satisfy a request.
Vary: Accept-Language tells a cache that this request header's value must match for reuse.
verify that both format and language survive the actual matching rules, or bypass caching until they do.
Vary does not change the URL, grant permission or override private/no-store.

answers.answer: A versioned asset URL changes when its bytes change. Publish app.v2.js with new bytes instead of overwriting app.v1.js; long caching fits assets whose bytes remain immutable at each URL. Update the referring page to request v2, recognizing an old cached page may still request v1. For a mutable page retaining its URL, choose freshness/revalidation to fit tolerated update delay, such as short freshness or validation on every reuse. A database update does not rewrite HTTP cached responses. A CDN purge removes or invalidates targeted CDN entries according to provider behavior. Check coverage of relevant URLs, variants and CDN layers plus propagation/completion behavior; do not assume instantaneous global replacement. CDN purge cannot evict a fresh browser copy or erase downloaded content. Unpublishing can stop future origin access and trigger purges but cannot instantly revoke already delivered public pages. Choose lifetimes knowing this limit. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: A versioned asset URL changes when its bytes change: publish app.v2.js instead of overwriting app.v1.js.
A database edit does not rewrite stored HTTP responses.
Verify coverage of the relevant URLs, variants and CDN cache layers, plus propagation and completion behavior.
Purging CDN entries does not evict fresh browser copies or erase downloaded content.

answers.answer: stale-while-revalidate allows bounded stale reuse while attempting background validation, hiding validation latency. stale-if-error permits bounded stale fallback on eligible errors, such as origin failure. These are optional permissions, not freshness or guaranteed availability. Freshness lasts 60 seconds; additional windows count from expiry. At age 75 the copy is 15 seconds stale, inside the 30-second background-validation window through age 90, so it can be served while refreshing. At age 150 it is 90 seconds stale: an eligible error permits fallback within the 120-second allowance through age 180. At age 200 it is 140 seconds stale, beyond both windows; neither directive authorizes stale reuse even with the same error. A cold cache has no stored fallback; exhausted allowances can expose failures. Verify support and policy. These directives cannot override private/no-store, and private-data correctness or urgent removal may disallow stale delivery despite public-help availability benefits. No lesson gap identified.

evidence.quote: The response is fresh for 60 seconds; stale windows start when freshness expires.
At age 200 neither extension still permits stale reuse.
A cold cache has no response to fall back to, and exhausted allowances can expose the failure.
Private-data correctness or urgent removal may forbid stale reuse even when it improves public-help availability.
